account:
Today has seemed mostly routine. I made my market visit, reviewed the town accounts, took tea with the neighbour, and remained available in my office this afternoon. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. I saw the baker restock the bread stall, and the neighbour said the innkeeper was tending supplies. I also noticed a lantern had been placed in the town hall near a long table; I do not know who placed it or why.

The only unusual news is the neighbour's report of rumours about a celebration or changes to the bridge. The neighbour had seen no evidence, and said the baker knew of no celebration. I have no basis for treating either rumour as a real plan, or connecting the lantern or ordinary stocking activity with them.

The secretary spent time verifying my tea address, which the neighbour has now confirmed as the cottage at (16, -60, 105), at three each day. That appears to have been appointment coordination rather than anything unusual. The secretary has now gone to ask the mill about concerns for tomorrow's grain inspection, at my request. I do not yet know the outcome. No correspondence has been brought to my attention, and the neighbour reported no dockside concerns. It is now 18:38, and I intend to go home for my scheduled evening at home.
